claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To begin, I need to know about the child (or children) you're claiming for.

**First question: How old is your child?**

This is important because:
- Children under 16 generally qualify automatically (with some conditions)
- Children aged 16-19 may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children aged 20 or over don't qualify

Please tell me:
1. Your child's name and age
2. If you have multiple children you want to claim for, please tell me about all of them

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 19 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about your son Alex, who is 19 years old and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 19 (which falls in the 16-19 age category), he may still qualify for Child Benefit, but we need to check if he meets the education or training requirements.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex currently in approved education or training, or has he recently left education?**

Please tell me which of these applies to Alex:

1. **Currently in approved education or training** - such as:
   - Full-time non-advanced education (A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQ Level 3 or below)
   - Approved vocational training programs
   - Studies at school or college

2. **Recently left education** - stopped studying within the last 20 weeks

3. **Neither** - not currently in education/training and either never was or left more than 20 weeks ago

Which situation describes Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is currently in education - he's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is studying A-levels at sixth form college, which is approved education. Now I need to verify that the education level qualifies for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! A-levels are approved, non-advanced education that qualifies for Child Benefit. Now I need to check a few more details about Alex's education:

**Questions about Alex's A-level studies:**

1. **Is his course full-time** (at least 12 hours per week of supervised study)?

2. **Is this education funded by an employer**, or does Alex have an agreement with an employer for a job after he finishes?

3. **Is Alex married or in a civil partnership?** (This only matters if yes, as married 16-19 year olds must be financially dependent on you to qualify)

Please let me know the answers to these questions.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
1. Yes, it's a full-time course at the college.

2. No, it's not funded by an employer and he doesn't have any job agreement lined up.

3. No, he's not married.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Alex's A-level course meets all the education requirements:
- ✓ A-levels are approved, non-advanced education
- ✓ Full-time course (12+ hours per week)
- ✓ Not employer-funded
- ✓ Not married

Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Does Alex work less than 24 hours per week (or is he not in paid work at all)?**

This is important because children aged 16+ who work 24 hours or more per week don't qualify for Child Benefit, even if they're in education.

Does Alex work:
- **Less than 24 hours per week**, or
- **Not in paid work at all**?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, Alex does work - he has a part-time job at the supermarket alongside his studies. He works full-time hours there, so it's more than 24 hours a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I see. This is an important point. Alex works more than 24 hours per week at the supermarket, which means he's working full-time alongside his A-level studies.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Unfortunately, based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Why Alex doesn't qualify:**

The rules state that young people aged 16 or over who work 24 or more hours per week do not qualify for Child Benefit, even if they are also in approved education like A-levels.

Since Alex is working full-time hours (more than 24 hours per week) at the supermarket, he doesn't meet the eligibility criteria.

**Important to note:**

- If Alex reduces his working hours to less than 24 hours per week while continuing his A-level studies, you would be able to claim Child Benefit for him again
- Once he completes or leaves his A-levels, if he's still working 24+ hours per week, he wouldn't qualify anyway (unless he starts other approved education/training and reduces his hours)

**Next steps:**

If Alex's work situation changes and he drops below 24 hours per week, you can make a new claim or restart your claim at that time.

Do you have any questions about this decision, or is there anything else I can help clarify?

Under the Child Benefit rules, children aged 16 or over who work 24 or more hours per week do not qualify for Child Benefit, even if they are in approved education. Therefore, Alex is ineligible.
